**bones 0.1.1 is on CRAN.** It was published on 16 October. It is my second
package on CRAN, after rewind.

```r
install.packages("bones")
```

bones gives Shiny outputs loading placeholders in the shape of their
content. [My first post](../2026-09-28-how-bones-began/index.qmd) explains
the idea. This one is about getting it through review.

I submitted 0.1.0 on 25 September. The automatic pre-tests on Windows and
Debian passed with one NOTE: "New submission". Every first submission gets
that note.

On 6 October, a reviewer sent two requests and ended with "Please fix and
resubmit."

## A package name keeps its case

CRAN asks for the names of packages, software and APIs in the Title and
Description fields of DESCRIPTION to be in single quotes. I had written
`'Shiny'`. The package is called `shiny`. Package names are case sensitive.

The title is now:

```text
Content-Shaped Loading Placeholders for 'shiny' Outputs
```

Title Case does not apply inside those quotes. The name must keep the
case of the package it names.

`R CMD check --as-cran` passed with `'Shiny'` and gave no note about it.
The human reviewer caught it. A clean check does not mean that every name
in the prose is right.

There was a second place to fix. Roxygen copies the Title and Description
into the package help page, `man/bones-package.Rd`, through the
`"_PACKAGE"` sentinel. Changing DESCRIPTION alone leaves the old text in
the help page and the PDF manual. I had to run roxygen again.

This shell command helps with the name check:

```sh
grep -oE "'[^']+'" DESCRIPTION | sort -u
```

It lists every quoted name. Compare each one with the real name, including
its case. Then rebuild the help files that copy those fields.

## Give the settings back, also under inst/

The other request was to restore changes to `par()`, `options()` and the
working directory in examples, vignettes and demos. The reviewer added
"in your inst folder".

bones has a demo app under `inst/examples/demo/`. Users can run it with:

```r
shiny::runApp(system.file("examples/demo", package = "bones"))
```

Its plots changed `par()` inside `renderPlot()` and never put the settings
back. `R CMD check` did not catch this either. The reviewer read `inst/`
by hand.

The fix saves the old settings and restores them when the function exits:

```r
old_par <- par(mar = c(3, 3, 1, 1), mgp = c(2, 0.6, 0), las = 1)
on.exit(par(old_par), add = TRUE)
```

`on.exit()` works inside a `renderPlot()` expression because Shiny makes
that expression the body of a function. The cleanup belongs to that
function, and also runs if it exits with an error.

A demo ships with the package too. I need to treat its changes to the
user's settings with the same care as changes in `R/`.

## Search beyond the line in the reply

The reviewer gave me an example, not a full list. Before resubmitting, I
searched the whole package for the same kind of change:

```sh
grep -rnE "options\(|par\(|setwd\(|Sys\.setenv\(" R man inst vignettes demo
```

The demo was the only place. But fixing only the named line would have
left me guessing about the rest. That is my first lesson from this
release: turn a review comment into a search for the pattern.

I fixed both requests and resubmitted as 0.1.1 on 6 October. A resubmission
needs a higher version. The covering comment starts with a "Resubmission"
section that lists each change.

Then it waited in CRAN's folder for new packages, called "newbies". I could
watch the queue at [CRAN incoming](https://cran.r-project.org/incoming/)
and on [cransays](https://r-hub.github.io/cransays/).

On 16 October, the reply was "Thanks, on its way to CRAN."
[bones 0.1.1](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=bones) was published that day.

## The release that tags itself

My second lesson is to let the GitHub release follow CRAN. A merge is too
early. CRAN can still send that version back. GitHub could then show
"Latest" beside a version CRAN never published. That nearly happened with
0.1.0.

A workflow in `.github/workflows/release.yaml`, first written for rewind,
runs once a day. It reads the bones version in the
[CRAN index](https://cloud.r-project.org/src/contrib/PACKAGES). If that
version has no git tag, it downloads the CRAN tarball.

It finds the oldest commit on main with that version in DESCRIPTION whose
files match the tarball. It skips DESCRIPTION, MD5 and `build/`, which
`R CMD build` and CRAN change. It tags that commit and makes a GitHub
release, using that version's section of NEWS.md as the notes.

On 17 October, it tagged v0.1.1 at the commit sent to CRAN. Main had already
moved on. Nobody had to remember to tag it.

Before a package reaches CRAN, the daily run stops with a notice instead
of an error. It does not send an email every day.

## What comes next

These changes are in the development version for 0.2.0. They are not on
CRAN yet:

- An error panel when an output fails, in place of Shiny's red error text.
- Learned shapes. After a load, the browser stores the content's shape,
  using numbers only, with no text. The next visit shows a skeleton in
  that shape.
- Clear errors for a misspelt shape. `type = "bars"` says
  `Did you mean "bar"?`.
